clauses.reason: Separate final semantic qualification from lightweight publication without changing authority.

updates.rationale: Repeated semantic review and synchronous tree deletion do not strengthen exact-source publication and dominate its latency.
updates.statement: Final fully validates source and review inputs and emits a versioned publication binding. Delivery verifies the frozen source, mutable local bindings, authorization and expected remote base without reconstructing source history or executing checks. Explicit final --deliver uses the same delivery owner after success. Publication succeeds independently of later maintenance cleanup; no cleanup worker or queue is required.

decisions.reason: Complete semantic review belongs to final. Repeating it during publication adds thousands of Git processes without new evidence when the frozen commit is unchanged. The publication binding retains exact immutable source and mutable local inputs; publication checks those identities and the atomic remote base. Cleanup is an independent maintenance outcome after publication, not a condition of delivery success. A background deletion design is unnecessary because existing maintenance cleanup already owns safe removal. Reopen if exact reviewed inputs or remote-first recovery cannot be established by the binding.

revision.summary: Final qualifies exact source; publication verifies its binding and cleanup runs separately.

transaction.reason: Apply the approved separation before implementation.
